text: What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download?

Abstract
We queried the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) for Series GSE309890 to determine the study’s scope and identify the downloadable processed files. Using a single GEO Series retrieval (functions.geo_series, list_files=true), we extracted metadata and enumerated supplementary files from the GEO FTP directory. The series is titled “Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback,” with organism Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655, experiment type “Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing,” platform GPL24659, 6 samples, and BioProject PRJNA1363958. The supplementary directory contains one compressed CSV file (“GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz”; size 510K; last modified 2025-11-14). No PubMed record is linked in GEO for this series at the time of retrieval. These results provide an actionable summary of study context and the exact processed dataset available for download, enabling downstream analysis (e.g., expression matrix import) without relying on additional E-utilities calls, as GEO stores processed values only in the supplementary files. Clear identification of the file, its format, and size supports reproducible data acquisition and informs pipeline selection for RNA-seq count/FPKM-level analyses.

I. Introduction
Background. GSE309890 is a GEO Series investigating how the SSRI sertraline influences the emergence of antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli, focusing on metabolic rewiring through the pentose phosphate pathway and the role of transketolase A (tktA). The RNA-seq-based expression profiling provides insight into stress-driven metabolic adaptations under sertraline exposure and their impact on resistance phenotypes.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. Prior to querying, the exact downloadable processed files and the series-level experimental context were unknown to the user.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: Retrieve the study description and list the downloadable processed files for GSE309890. Hypothesis: GEO will host at least one processed expression matrix in the series’ supplementary directory, and the series metadata will specify organism, platform, and sample composition.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We selected GEO Series metadata to directly resolve the study’s scope and the exact processed files. GEO stores processed expression matrices under “supplementary_files” on its FTP tree; thus, fetching series-level metadata and the supplementary directory listing was the most efficient route.
Materials.
- NCBI GEO (queried via functions.geo_series).
Procedures.
- functions.geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true)
  • This call returns GEO Series metadata (title, summary, organism, experiment type, platform, sample list, BioProject) and lists the supplementary files in the FTP directory for GSE309890.
Statistical Analysis.
- Counts reported were taken directly from returned fields:
  • sample_count from record.sample_count (n=6).
  • supplementary file count from the length of supplementary_files (n=1).
  • File size and last-modified from supplementary_files metadata.
- No deduplication was needed; the series and file listings are authoritative and unique in GEO’s directory.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1. GSE309890 overview

|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| Title                     | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the PPP: tktA enables metabolic rollback |
| Organism                  | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655                                                        |
| Experiment type           | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing                                               |
| Platform                  | GPL24659                                                                                         |
| Sample count              | 6                                                                                                |
| BioProject                | PRJNA1363958                                                                                     |
| Date public               | 2026/02/01                                                                                       |
| GEO page                  | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890                                    |
| FTP directory             | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/                                     |
| Supplementary file types  | CSV                                                                                              |
| Supplementary file count  | 1                                                                                                |
| Supplementary directory   | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/                              |

Table 2. Samples in GSE309890
| GSM accession | Title                                   |
|---------------|------------------------------------------|
| GSM9284462    | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep3 |
| GSM9284459    | E. coli, control,rep3                    |
| GSM9284457    | E. coli, control,rep1                    |
| GSM9284460    | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep1 |
| GSM9284461    | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep2 |
| GSM9284458    | E. coli, control,rep2                    |

Table 3. Supplementary files available for download
| File name                         | URL                                                                                                             | Size  | Last modified        |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------|----------------------|
| GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz             | 510K  | 2025-11-14 11:10     |

Findings.
- The series includes 6 RNA-seq samples.
- One supplementary file is available for download: a compressed CSV containing FPKMs for all samples.
- No PubMed record is linked to the series in GEO at the time of retrieval.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The study centers on sertraline-induced metabolic rewiring in E. coli and its effect on antibiotic resistance, with RNA-seq profiling across 6 samples. The single downloadable processed file (FPKM matrix) provides sample-level expression estimates suitable for downstream analyses such as differential expression or pathway-level summary without requiring raw FASTQ retrieval from SRA/ENA.
Context. The returned GEO metadata specifies organism, platform, and sample composition, and the supplementary directory lists the only processed expression matrix (FPKMs) available for direct download. GEO’s note that processed values exist only in supplementary files is consistent with the presence of a single CSV.gz file.
Limitations.
- GEO’s API provides metadata only; processed values must be downloaded from the FTP supplementary directory.
- No PubMed linkage is registered, which may indicate unpublished or not-yet-indexed status; this does not imply absence of data.
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 provides a single processed FPKM matrix covering 6 E. coli samples under sertraline exposure and controls. The next query worth running is to resolve and list raw sequencing runs for BioProject PRJNA1363958 (e.g., via ENA/SRA study lookup) if raw data are needed for re-quantification or alternative normalization. On request, we can generate a downloadable TSV file summarizing the series metadata and file links shown above.

References
[1] NCBI GEO Series page for GSE309890: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO FTP directory (series root): https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[3] NCBI GEO FTP supplementary directory: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
[4] NCBI E-utilities esummary endpoint (GDS): https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi
[5] Supplementary file URL: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz

Acknowledgments
We acknowledge NCBI GEO and NCBI E-utilities for series metadata and file listings, and NCBI’s FTP service for the processed expression file hosting.
